Designing a reliable file backup system requires a shift in mindset from simply "copying files" to implementing a **data resilience strategy**. The goal is not just to have a copy of your data, but to ensure that you can recover that data quickly and completely regardless of the failure scenario (hardware crash, ransomware, or natural disaster).

Designing a reliable file backup system requires a shift in mindset from "making copies" to "building a recovery infrastructure." A backup is only reliable if it can be proven to work through restoration.

Here is a comprehensive guide to designing a professional-grade file backup system.

---

### 1. Backup Strategies: Full vs. Incremental
A reliable system rarely relies on a single method; it uses a hybrid approach to balance storage efficiency with recovery speed.

#### Full Backups
A full backup copies all selected files and folders.
*   **Pros:** Simplest to restore; every backup is a complete snapshot of the data.
